B: Hiya! Oh my god, it's you! You look so much like my supervisor, it's actually mad.
A: So I've heard. Kelly told me. I hope he's alright, your supervisor.
B: He's lovely! Proper calm. So yeah, it's a compliment. I'm Ellie.
A: Darren. The other one.
B: The leisure centre Darren! So you're a duty manager?
A: Yeah, in Taunton. Started as a lifeguard, about twenty-five years back. Worked my way up, slowly.
B: That's literally what I want to do. I'm doing my Level 2 swim teaching this year, and then maybe duty manager one day. Or go abroad. Or be a paramedic. I haven't decided.
A: Plenty of time. Get your Level 2 done, get your pool plant if they'll put you on it. That's the bit that helps you move up, knowing the plant room.
B: Oh, is it? I've never really been in ours, like, properly. It's all pipes and smells weird.
A: That'll be the chlorine. Ask your duty manager if you can shadow a water test. Most of them are glad of the help.
B: Okay, I'm going to. That's proper useful, thank you. Did you have a code brown this week? We had one Friday, the whole pool shut for an hour.
A: Ha. We get one most weeks. We were shut two days last week, though, the boiler went.
B: Two days! People must've gone mad.
A: They did. One bloke rang four times to ask if it was open yet. Same answer every time.
B: We've got an old man like that, comes every morning at seven on the dot. He'd be outside banging on the doors.
A: Every centre's got one.
B: Have you ever had to do, like, a proper rescue? I did one last summer, a teenage lad in the deep end. It was so quick, I still think about it sometimes.
A: Yeah, a few, over the years. It's always quicker than you expect. You did your job, though. He's alright?
B: Yeah, he's fine. His mum brought a card in.
A: There you go. That's the bit to hang on to. You'll go over it for a while, and then you'll go over it less. That's about it really.
B: Yeah. That's kind of what my nan says. Sorry, that got a bit deep! Do you swim yourself still?
A: Few lengths before a shift. Five-a-side Thursdays. Walk the dog, Pip, along the canal.
B: Aw. Mine's called Biscuit, which apparently is the name of every animal in this group.
A: So I gather. Pip's going deaf, mind. I could call her Biscuit and she wouldn't notice.
B: Ha! Do you get to Glastonbury and stuff? You look like a festival person.
A: Been three times. Last one was 2019. Claire reckons I'm too old now.
